items.title: Check one rule
items.text:
topology-checker <group> <rule> <input> [--layer NAME] [--other INPUT] [--other-layer NAME] [-o OUTPUT]

topology-checker line must-not-have-dangles roads.gpkg --layer roads -o errors.gpkg
topology-checker point must-be-covered-by-lines stops.geojson --other routes.gpkg

Groups are point, line, polygon and geometry. See Rules. Without --layer, each layer in the input is checked separately. Two-layer rules check every input layer against every --other layer.

items.title: Check a topology definition
items.text:
tolerance = 0.001

[layers]
roads = { path = "city.gpkg", layer = "roads" }
stops = { path = "stops.geojson" }

[[rules]]
rule = "line/must-not-have-dangles"
layer = "roads"

[[rules]]
rule = "point/must-be-covered-by-lines"
layer = "stops"
other = "roads"

topology-checker validate topology.toml -o errors.gpkg

tolerance and layer are optional. Paths are relative to the TOML file. Unknown keys are errors.

items.title: Tolerance and CRS
items.text:
Tolerance is in coordinate units, and calculations are planar. --tolerance overrides the TOML value. If neither is set, the default depends on the CRS:

  • projected CRS: 1 mm;
  • geographic CRS: 1e-8 degrees;
  • unknown CRS, or any input without one: 0.

Within the tolerance, coordinates are treated as coincident, so a near miss within tolerance is a touch, not a dangle or an overlap. Set the tolerance to the data's positional precision. Tolerance 0 is exact on the binary coordinates, so floating-point slivers become reportable.

Inputs must share a CRS; the CLI does not reproject. GeoJSON without a crs member is EPSG:4326. A geographic CRS with a nonzero tolerance prints a warning, because calculations are planar.

items.title: Output files
items.text:
-o writes errors_point, errors_line and errors_polygon layers. The format comes from the file extension or from --driver; topology-checker drivers --write lists the formats. Nothing is written when there are no violations. An existing file needs --overwrite.

Columns: violation_id, rule, error_type, origin_layer, origin_fid, origin_part, destination_layer, destination_fid, destination_part. A violation with several geometry types gets a row in each layer, with the same violation_id. Shapefiles shorten the names to viol_id, orig_layer, orig_part, dest_layer, dest_fid and dest_part.

items.title: Output and exit codes
items.text:
• stdout: a summary table, or the report as JSON with --json. With --summary, the JSON leaves out the list of violations and keeps the counts.
  • stderr: warnings, and any error. With --json, an error is printed as {"error": "..."}. validate --progress also prints checked rule K/N (<rule>): C errors as each rule finishes.
Exit code Meaning 0 No violations 1 Violations found 2 Error

items.title: Other commands
items.text:
topology-checker rules                    # add --json for JSON
topology-checker drivers --read --write
topology-checker utilities merge-lines roads.gpkg --layer roads -o merged.gpkg
topology-checker utilities explode-lines roads.gpkg --layer roads -o segments.gpkg

merge-lines joins lines at endpoints shared by exactly two lines. explode-lines splits lines into single segments.

items.title: CLI
items.text:
Requires Rust 1.88 or newer.

cargo install topology-checker --locked

This build reads and writes GeoJSON, GeoPackage, Shapefile, FlatGeobuf, GeoParquet, KML and GPX without GDAL. For other formats, add GDAL:

# Build GDAL from source (needs CMake, a C/C++ compiler and sqlite3)
CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 cargo install topology-checker --locked --features gdal
# Use an installed GDAL
cargo install topology-checker --locked --features gdal-system

items.title: Python
items.text:
pip install "topology-checker[io]"

This adds Shapely, GeoPandas and CRS support. For WKB input and output only, with no dependencies:

pip install topology-checker

Python 3.10 to 3.14. See Python usage.

items.title: QGIS
items.text: Install Topology Rules in Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins (QGIS 3.34 or newer). Its panel installs the Python package, or runs the CLI (0.2.0 or newer). See QGIS plugin.

items.title: Web app
items.text:
Requires Node.js and Rust 1.88 or newer.

npm ci --prefix web
npm run build --prefix web
cargo build -p topology-checker-web --release --locked

The frontend is embedded in target/release/topology-checker-web. See Web app.

items.title: RustGIS plugin
items.text: topology-checker is a plugin for RustGIS. Download topology-checker-<version>.rgplugin from the latest release, then in RustGIS open the Plugin Manager and choose Install from File. Do not unzip the file. See RustGIS plugin, which also covers building it from source.

items.title: ReportStream
items.text:
ReportStream(native: NativeReportStream, layers: tuple[Layer, ...], specs: tuple[RuleSpec, ...], crs: tuple[CRS | None, tuple[str, ...]])

Bases: Iterator[RuleReport]

Yield each rule's report as soon as that rule finishes, in rule order.

Reports equal validate().rules. Use a context manager or close() when stopping early; closing cancels the remaining rules. The worker owns immutable snapshots. Final summary is available only after successful exhaustion, and is None after early close.

items.title: Python usage
items.text: Install with pip install "topology-checker[io]" for Shapely geometries, GeoPandas input and export, and CRS metadata. pip install topology-checker has no dependencies and works with WKB only. Python 3.10 through 3.14 on regular CPython are supported. Wheels need no Rust installation. See the API reference for every class and function.

items.title: Register and validate
items.text:
import geopandas as gpd
from topology_checker import Rule, Topology

roads_gdf = gpd.read_file("roads.gpkg")
topology = Topology(tolerance=0.001)
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_HAVE_DANGLES, roads_gdf)
report = topology.validate()
errors = report.to_geodataframe()
print(report.is_valid, report.error_count, report.warnings)

add_rule accepts a Shapely geometry, a sequence of geometries or WKB items, a GeoSeries, a GeoDataFrame, a GeoJSON mapping, or an object with __geo_interface__. Pass the second layer with the keyword argument other=. Use enum members such as Rule.MUST_NOT_OVERLAP; parse serialized names with Rule("must-not-overlap") before registration.

Each raw input creates a fresh XY snapshot at registration. Later edits to a GeoDataFrame or list do not change that layer. Passing the same raw object to two rules creates two layers, and a generator is consumed on each call. validate() returns an immutable report snapshot; topology violations are results, while invalid registrations raise exceptions and leave the topology unchanged.

items.title: Reuse a layer explicitly
items.text:
from shapely.geometry import LineString
from topology_checker import Rule, Topology

topology = Topology(tolerance=0.001)
roads = topology.add_layer(
    [LineString([(0, 0), (1, 0)]), LineString([(1, 0), (2, 0)])],
    name="roads",
    fids=[41, 92],
    crs="EPSG:28992",
)
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_HAVE_DANGLES, roads)
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, roads)
report = topology.validate()
print(topology.layer(roads).name)
print(report.to_dict())

The returned LayerId belongs to its originating Topology. Reuse it across rules to share the registered layer and native caches. Binary rules require distinct IDs. A RuleSpec returned by add_rule also exposes the registered IDs through .layer and .other.

FIDs default to original input positions, independent of a GeoDataFrame's index or GeoJSON feature IDs. Explicit FIDs must be unique signed 64-bit integers, one per original position, including positions subsequently skipped. Reports preserve FID and multipart provenance in .origin and .destination. Missing and empty features are skipped with warnings, extra dimensions are discarded, and nonfinite retained XY coordinates are rejected. Mixed nonempty families are accepted only by rules with an ANY input signature.

items.title: WKB input and output
items.text:
import struct
from topology_checker import Rule, Topology

def line(*coords):
    header = struct.pack("<BII", 1, 2, len(coords))
    return header + b"".join(struct.pack("<dd", x, y) for x, y in coords)

topology = Topology(tolerance=0.001)
roads = topology.add_layer([line((0, 0), (1, 0)), line((1, 0), (2, 0))], fids=[41, 92])
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_HAVE_DANGLES, roads)
for violation in topology.validate().violations:
    print(violation.origin, violation.wkb.hex())

WKB items are bytes, bytearray or memoryview in ISO or extended WKB, either byte order; None is a missing feature. Unreadable WKB raises ValueError naming the layer and FID. Violation.wkb and Layer.wkb are 2D little-endian ISO WKB. Violation.geometry and Layer.geometries decode them with Shapely.

items.title: Declare ambiguous empty layers
items.text:
from topology_checker import GeometryKind, Rule, Topology

topology = Topology()
empty_lines = topology.add_layer([], kind=GeometryKind.LINE)
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, empty_lines)
assert topology.validate().is_valid

Family inference uses nonempty parts first, then empty geometry hints. An empty list, only missing values, or conflicting empty hints have no inferred family. Rules with multiple possible signatures then require a declaration through add_layer(..., kind=GeometryKind.POINT), LINE, or POLYGON. A declaration must agree with every retained nonempty part. A uniquely matching rule, such as MUST_NOT_HAVE_DANGLES, can resolve even with unknown empty input.

items.title: CRS and tolerance
items.text:
The engine operates in a Cartesian XY plane. It does not reproject, calculate geodesic distances, or infer a CRS from coordinates. Reproject geographic data to an appropriate projected CRS before using distance tolerances.

Tolerance is finite, nonnegative, and expressed in the inputs' coordinate units. For a CRS using metres, 0.001 is one millimetre. It is interpreted by each rule, such as a distance threshold, a minimum retained line length, or a polygon sliver filter. It does not apply a universal geometry buffer or repair geometries. Inspect the concrete rule description for the relevant behavior.

Within the tolerance, coordinates are treated as coincident, so a near miss within tolerance is a touch, not a dangle or an overlap. Set the tolerance to the data's positional precision. Tolerance 0 is exact on the binary coordinates, so floating-point slivers become reportable.

All known layer CRSs must agree. Explicit CRS metadata must agree with metadata on the input. Unknown CRSs are accepted as caller-supplied coordinates. When known and unknown metadata are mixed, validation continues with a warning and the export CRS is unset. crs=, to_dict() with violations and Report.to_geodataframe() require the io extra.

items.title: Geometry-dependent semantics
items.text:
The 24 public constraints resolve to the 38 concrete rules using the ordered geometry families and whether other= is supplied. These examples illustrate why the concrete variant matters:

Public rule and inputs Meaning MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, points Coincident point pairs within tolerance. MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, lines Shared linework between distinct features; crossings and self-overlaps are excluded. MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, polygons Shared areas between distinct features, excluding slivers below tolerance. MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, lines then polygons Interior or shared boundary line pieces longer than tolerance; isolated contacts are allowed. MUST_BE_INSIDE, points then polygons Strict interior membership; boundary proximity within tolerance is outside. MUST_BE_INSIDE, lines then polygons Pieces outside the polygon union longer than tolerance; boundary linework is covered. MUST_NOT_INTERSECT, lines Overlaps and interior crossings between distinct features; endpoint touches are allowed. MUST_NOT_INTERSECT, lines then polygons Interior pieces, shared boundary pieces and isolated contacts, including boundary proximity within tolerance. MUST_NOT_HAVE_GAPS, polygons Enclosed gaps and an outer-boundary diagnostic; inspect error categories. MUST_NOT_BE_CONTAINED_BY, any then any Whole cleaned features contained by individual targets, excluding mutual containment; no tolerance buffer.

Order matters: line then polygon signatures do not imply polygon then line support. Multipart parts of one feature retain their FID; use the dedicated self-intersection or self-overlap constraints to examine a feature internally.

from shapely.geometry import Point, box
from topology_checker import Rule, Topology

topology = Topology()
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_BE_INSIDE, [Point(0.5, 0.5)], other=[box(0, 0, 1, 1)])
result = topology.validate().rules[0]
print(result.resolved_rule.value)
print(result.resolved_rule.description)
for variant in Rule.MUST_NOT_OVERLAP.variants:
    print(variant.inputs, variant.description)

Use .resolved_rule on a RuleSpec, RuleReport, or Violation to inspect the selected semantics. Invalid arity, unsupported families, or ambiguous empty inputs are reported at registration with the supported signatures.

items.title: Line utilities
items.text:
from shapely.geometry import LineString
from topology_checker import explode_lines, merge_lines

lines = [LineString([(0, 0), (1, 0)]), LineString([(1, 0), (2, 0)])]
merged = merge_lines(lines, tolerance=0.001)
segments = explode_lines(merged)
assert len(segments) == 2

Both utilities accept the same inputs as add_layer and operate on planar snapshots. They return tuples of Shapely lines, or of WKB bytes when every input is WKB.

items.title: Input validity and tolerance
items.text:
Polygon registration rejects self-intersections, closing spikes, crossing or nested holes, and overlapping, nested, or edge-sharing parts of a MultiPolygon. Empty members and degenerate rings are cleaned first. Errors identify the layer, original FID, part, ring, and reason. Registration is atomic. Repair data explicitly before registration if needed; the validator preserves original coordinates.

A line part whose original vertices all lie within the tolerance of each other is collapsed. It contributes no edges to line graphs built with that tolerance and receives one warning identifying its layer, FID, and original part. Warnings appear in warnings() and reports. Closed parts have no endpoints. In the line MUST_NOT_INTERSECT and MUST_NOT_INTERSECT_OR_TOUCH_INTERIOR rules, a feature's endpoints are where an odd number of its open parts end (OGC mod-2); dangle, pseudo-node and endpoint rules use every open part end. A polygon-boundary crossing within tolerance of an open part endpoint is exempt from MUST_NOT_CROSS_BOUNDARIES; closed parts have no exemption. Boundary intervals pass MUST_BE_INSIDE, fail MUST_BE_PROPERLY_INSIDE, and are reported as lines by intersection rules.

Polygon overlaps and gaps pass the sliver test when their positive area and perimeter satisfy 2 * area / perimeter >= tolerance. Perimeter includes hole boundaries. Zero tolerance retains positive-area decisions. CRS compatibility ignores axis order, so EPSG:4326 and OGC:CRS84 can share a topology. Projection, datum, and unit differences still require reprojection.

items.title: Stream validation
items.text:
with topology.iter_validate(batch_size=1024) as stream:
    for violation in stream:
        print(violation.error_type, violation.origin)
    summary = stream.summary
    print(summary.error_count, summary.warnings)

The stream captures immutable layer and rule snapshots. It yields aggregated violations in rule, category, and feature order, preserving every duplicate pair. Use the context manager or close() when stopping early. Closing cancels native work and releases queued geometry. summary is available after successful exhaustion and stays None after cancellation or failure. validate() and its Report remain eager and compatible. Large duplicate stacks still produce a quadratic number of pairs, so stream them when the complete report is too large for memory.

with topology.iter_reports() as reports:
    for rule in reports:
        print(rule.resolved_rule.value, len(rule.violations))

iter_reports() yields each rule's RuleReport as soon as that rule finishes, in registration order, and otherwise behaves like iter_validate().

Polygon area and boundary decisions retain exact node identities until output. The inclusive area-to-perimeter threshold is certified before geometry emission, with exact rational calculations for cancellation and ambiguous thresholds. Original vertices stay fixed. Intersection nodes share one output coordinate; a local search preserves their topology within at most 16 floating-point steps and 100,000 candidate assignments per affected neighborhood.

An unsatisfied output constraint raises topology_checker.PrecisionError, a RuntimeError subclass. Its message identifies the operation, rule, and available layer and FID context. Eager validation returns no partial report. A failed stream raises the same exception and leaves summary as None.

items.title: QGIS plugin
items.text: Topology Rules adds the rules of topology-checker to QGIS. It runs the checks in the Python package or the CLI, and includes neither. Each rule is a Processing tool, and a panel runs several rules at once and lists their errors.

items.title: Install
items.text:
1. In QGIS 3.34 or newer, open Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins and install Topology Rules.
  2. Install the Python package or the CLI:
    • Install Python package… in the panel's menu. It first shows the file, its size, URL and SHA-256. Then it downloads the file from PyPI, checks the SHA-256 and unpacks the package into python/dependencies/topology_rules/<version> in the QGIS profile. Installs nothing else. Each step goes to the Topology Rules log tab and to install.log. Needs Python 3.10 or newer, on Windows x64, macOS, or Linux x86_64. A new plugin version offers its package version; QGIS loads it after a restart.
    • The CLI, 0.2.0 or newer, such as from cargo install topology-checker --locked. The plugin finds it on the PATH or in Cargo's bin folder; otherwise choose it in the panel, or set its path under Settings > Options > Processing > Providers > Topology Rules.

items.title: Python package by hand
items.text:
Use the Python of QGIS. <profile> is the folder that Settings > User Profiles > Open Active Profile Folder opens, and <version> is the plugin version. The panel shows the exact command.

Windows, in the OSGeo4W Shell:

python -m pip install --no-deps --target "<profile>\python\dependencies\topology_rules\<version>" topology-checker==<version>

macOS, in Terminal:

/Applications/QGIS.app/Contents/MacOS/python -m pip install --no-deps --target "<profile>/python/dependencies/topology_rules/<version>" topology-checker==<version>

Linux, with pip (for example the python3-pip package):

python3 -m pip install --no-deps --target "<profile>/python/dependencies/topology_rules/<version>" topology-checker==<version>

items.title: Panel
items.text:
Open Topology Rules from the Vector menu or the toolbar.

  1. Pick a layer and a rule, then Add rule. Rules that compare two layers also ask for the other layer. Repeat for more rules.
  2. Run checks all the ticked rules in one pass.

The gear button next to ? sets the engine for the panel and the Processing tools: Automatic (the Python package where QGIS can use it, else the CLI), Python package or Executable. Its menu also installs, updates or removes the Python package, and has Choose executable…. With only the CLI, the panel offers the package once.

The errors are a tree by rule and kind. Selecting one zooms to it, highlights it and filters the map to its group. Select features selects the features an error is about, and Ignore error hides an error until you stop ignoring it, also in later runs.

Style in the gear menu sets how errors are drawn in every project, Processing outputs included: Colour by rule and layer, rule, layer or one colour; Size small, normal or large; Colour ramp the default or any saved ramp, with Invert and Edit…. Invalid geometries stay red; no other group gets a colour near it. Reset style restores the default.

Under Options, Selected features only and Only the visible extent limit the layer each rule checks, not the layer it is checked against. Export… writes the ticked rules as a topology.toml for the CLI, saving layers that are not files of their own in a GeoPackage next to it. Import… reads one. The list, the options and the ignored errors are saved with the project.

items.title: Processing
items.text:
Each rule is a tool named after it, such as Lines must not have dangles, in the Topology Rules provider, grouped as Points, Lines, Polygons and All geometries. It adds the errors to the project as point, line and polygon layers. With Selected features only, only the selected features are checked. The second layer of a two-layer rule is reprojected to the CRS of the first.

Check topology definition runs a topology.toml. The tools also run without a window:

qgis_process run topologyrules:line_must_not_have_dangles --INPUT=roads.gpkg --ERRORS_POINT=errors.gpkg

items.title: Tolerance and invalid geometries
items.text:
The tolerance is in the units of the first layer's CRS. Left empty, it is the CLI default for that CRS: see Tolerance and CRS.

Features the tool cannot read, such as invalid polygons or coordinates that are not finite, are left out of the run and listed as errors of their own.

items.title: Develop
items.text:
Lint needs no QGIS: in qgis_plugin/, uv sync, then uv run ruff check . and uv run ruff format --check ..

pyright and the tests need a QGIS Python. With Docker, as CI does (--platform makes it work on ARM machines too):

docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v "$PWD":/src -w /src rust:1 cargo build --release -p topology-checker --target-dir target/linux
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v "$PWD":/src -w /src/qgis_plugin -e TOPOLOGY_CHECKER=/src/target/linux/release/topology-checker -e UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/venv qgis/qgis:stable \
  bash -c 'pip install --break-system-packages uv && uv venv /tmp/venv --system-site-packages --python /usr/bin/python3 && uv sync --locked && uv run pyright && uv run pytest'

Tests that need the tool skip without TOPOLOGY_CHECKER. With a local QGIS, run cargo build --release and point TOPOLOGY_CHECKER at target/release/topology-checker:

  • macOS (checked), with your QGIS app, e.g. /Applications/QGIS-final-4_2_2.app: uv pip install --target /tmp/qgis-pytest pytest pytest-qgis, then APP=/Applications/QGIS-final-4_2_2.app/Contents; PYTHONHOME=$APP/Frameworks PYTHONPATH=/tmp/qgis-pytest QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen TOPOLOGY_CHECKER=<absolute path to target/release/topology-checker> $APP/MacOS/python3.12 -m pytest. pyright does not run on that Python; use Docker.
  • Linux and Windows (not checked here): uv venv --system-site-packages --python <QGIS's python> (/usr/bin/python3, or python in the OSGeo4W shell), uv sync --locked, then uv run pytest and uv run pyright.

The modules are listed in qgis_plugin/topology_rules/__init__.py.

items.title: Rules
items.text: Run a rule as topology-checker <group> <rule>, or use rule = "<group>/<rule>" in topology.toml. topology-checker <group> <rule> --help prints the exact semantics.

items.title: Points (10)
items.text: Rule Needs Description ArcGIS QGIS point/must-not-overlap one point layer Find duplicate points within the inclusive Euclidean distance tolerance. Must Be Disjoint Must not have duplicates point/must-not-overlap-with two point layers Find duplicate points across two layers within the inclusive Euclidean distance tolerance. point/must-be-inside point layer + polygon layer Find points outside the polygons, including points on or within the distance tolerance of their edges. Must Be Properly Inside Polygons Must be inside point/must-be-covered-by-lines point layer + line layer Find points without linework within the inclusive distance tolerance, including line endpoints. Must Be Covered By (Point-Line) Must be covered by point/must-be-covered-by-line-endpoints point layer + line layer Find points without a covering open line endpoint. Line parts closed within tolerance have no endpoints. Must Be Covered By Endpoint Of Must be covered by endpoints of point/must-be-covered-by-polygon-boundaries point layer + polygon layer Find points away from polygon edges, including holes and shared parcel edges. Must Be Covered By Boundary Of (Point-Area) point/must-be-covered-by-polygons point layer + polygon layer Find points outside polygon areas and farther than the tolerance from their edges. Boundary points are allowed. point/must-not-be-inside-polygons point layer + polygon layer Find points strictly inside polygons. Points on or within tolerance of their edges are allowed. point/must-not-intersect-lines point layer + line layer Find points touching linework anywhere within the inclusive distance tolerance, including endpoints. point/must-not-intersect-polygons point layer + polygon layer Find points inside polygons or touching their edges within tolerance.

items.title: Lines (19)
items.text: Rule Needs Description ArcGIS QGIS line/must-not-have-dangles one line layer Find unconnected line endpoints. Must Not Have Dangles Must not have dangles line/must-not-have-pseudo-nodes one line layer Find joins connecting exactly two distinct features at their endpoints. Closed loops are allowed. Must Not Have Pseudo Nodes Must not have pseudo nodes line/must-not-overlap one line layer Find shared line segments between distinct features. Crossings, branches ending within tolerance and overlaps within one feature are excluded. Must Not Overlap line/must-not-overlap-with two line layers Find shared line segments across two layers. Crossings and branches ending within tolerance are excluded. Must Not Overlap With line/must-not-self-overlap one line layer Find line segments traced more than once by the same feature, including across its parts. Parts branching off at an angle are excluded. Must Not Self-Overlap line/must-not-intersect one line layer Find overlaps and crossings between distinct features away from their endpoints. Endpoint touches are allowed. A multipart line's endpoints are where an odd number of its parts end. Must Not Intersect line/must-not-intersect-with two line layers Find overlaps and crossings across two layers away from their endpoints. Endpoint touches are allowed. A multipart line's endpoints are where an odd number of its parts end. Must Not Intersect With line/must-not-intersect-or-touch-interior one line layer Find overlaps, crossings and endpoint touches on the interior of another feature. Touches only at both features' endpoints are allowed. A multipart line's endpoints are where an odd number of its parts end. Must Not Intersect Or Touch Interior line/must-not-intersect-or-touch-interior-with two line layers Find overlaps, crossings and endpoint touches on a line's interior across two layers. Touches only at both features' endpoints are allowed. A multipart line's endpoints are where an odd number of its parts end. Must Not Intersect Or Touch Interior With line/must-not-self-intersect one line layer Find overlaps and crossings within one feature. Closed loops and self-touches are allowed. Must Not Self-Intersect line/must-be-inside line layer + polygon layer Find line pieces outside the polygons and farther than the distance tolerance from their exterior or hole edges. Every remaining outside piece is reported, including short tails. Must Be Inside line/endpoints-must-be-covered-by-points line layer + point layer Find open line endpoints without a covering point. Line parts closed within tolerance have no endpoints. Endpoint Must Be Covered By End points must be covered by line/must-be-covered-by-polygon-boundaries line layer + polygon layer Find line pieces farther than tolerance from polygon exterior or hole edges. Report every uncovered portion, including short tails. Must Be Covered By Boundary Of (Line-Area) line/must-not-cross-polygon-boundaries line layer + polygon layer Find lines entering or leaving polygons through exterior or hole edges. Tangencies, endpoint touches and shared segments are allowed. line/must-be-properly-inside-polygons line layer + polygon layer Find whole line parts that leave polygon coverage or come within tolerance of its boundary. Gaps narrower than the tolerance are closed, except where polygons face each other only at corners, and may close up to 10% over it where they widen to an open end. line/must-not-overlap-with-polygons line layer + polygon layer Find line pieces inside polygons or along their edges, longer than tolerance. Isolated contacts are allowed. line/must-not-overlap-polygon-boundaries line layer + polygon layer Find line pieces shared with polygon edges, longer than tolerance. Crossings and isolated contacts are allowed. line/must-not-intersect-polygons line layer + polygon layer Find any line contact with polygons, including interior pieces, shared edges and isolated touches within tolerance. line/endpoints-must-be-covered-by-polygon-boundaries line layer + polygon layer Find open line endpoints away from polygon exterior or hole edges. Line parts closed within tolerance have no endpoints.

items.title: Polygons (7)
items.text: Rule Needs Description ArcGIS QGIS polygon/must-not-overlap one polygon layer Find shared areas between distinct polygon features, ignoring slivers below the tolerance. Must Not Overlap Must not overlap polygon/must-not-overlap-with two polygon layers Find shared polygon areas across two layers, ignoring slivers below the tolerance. Must Not Overlap With Must not overlap with polygon/must-not-have-gaps one polygon layer Find enclosed gaps between polygons, ignoring sliver gaps below the tolerance. Also report outer boundaries separately. Must Not Have Gaps Must not have gaps polygon/boundaries-must-be-covered-by-lines polygon layer + line layer Find polygon exterior or hole edges farther than tolerance from lines. Report every uncovered portion, including short tails. Boundary Must Be Covered By (Area-Line) polygon/must-contain-point polygon layer + point layer Find polygons without a strictly interior point feature. All parts of a point feature must qualify. Contains Point Must contain polygon/must-contain-one-point polygon layer + point layer Find polygons and point features without a one-to-one interior assignment. Count feature IDs, including multipart features. Contains One Point polygon/must-not-contain-points polygon layer + point layer Find strictly contained points, with the polygon as the primary feature. Boundary points are allowed.

items.title: All geometries (2)
items.text: Rule Needs Description ArcGIS QGIS geometry/must-not-be-multipart one layer of any geometry type Find features with more than one part. A Multi geometry with only one part is allowed. Must Be Single Part (lines) Must not have multi-part geometries geometry/must-not-be-contained-by two layers of any geometry type Find whole features contained by an individual feature in the other layer. Equal geometries are allowed. No tolerance buffer is used. Check Geometry (Contained)

items.title: RustGIS plugin
items.text: topology-checker is available as a plugin for RustGIS, the open-source desktop GIS. It runs as a sandboxed WebAssembly plugin built on the same engine as the CLI and Python, and adds one tool for each of the 38 rules.

items.title: Install
items.text:
1. Download topology-checker-<version>.rgplugin from the latest release. Do not unzip it.
  2. In RustGIS open the Plugin Manager and choose Install from File.
  3. Pick the .rgplugin file. The plugin asks for no permissions.

The tools appear on a Topology ribbon tab, grouped as Points, Lines, Polygons and Geometry, each with a menu for rules on one layer and a menu for rules that compare two layers. They are also listed with RustGIS's other geoprocessing tools as plugin:topology-checker/<tool>.

items.title: Use a tool
items.text:
Each tool takes the layer to check, a second layer for the rules that compare two, and a tolerance. Tool ids are the rule names with the slash replaced by a hyphen: polygon/must-not-have-gaps is polygon-must-not-have-gaps.

  • If the layer has a selection, only the selected features are checked.
  • Features without geometry are skipped.
  • The result is a new layer named <layer>: <rule>. Each feature is a violation with rule, error_type, origin_fid, origin_part, destination_fid and destination_part. origin_fid is the source feature's row when RustGIS provides one, else its position in the checked features. Clean data adds no layer.
  • Messages list the violation counts and any warnings, such as line parts that collapsed under the tolerance.
  • Choosing the same layer twice for a two-layer rule is an error.

items.title: Tolerance
items.text: RustGIS gives tools longitude and latitude, and the engine is planar, so the tolerance is in degrees. The default, 0.000001, is about 11 cm at the equator. A degree of longitude is shorter away from the equator, so tolerances are not equal in every direction. Use the CLI or Python on projected data when you need a tolerance in metres.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
The plugin runs in a RustGIS sandbox with 512 MB of memory and an instruction budget per tool run. In a smoke test through the plugin interface in Node, 10,000 polygons took about 0.4 s for the overlap rule and 170 MB peak. Layers of several hundred thousand features may exceed the sandbox limits. Use the CLI for those.

Invalid polygons are rejected with the feature and ring, as in the other front ends.

items.title: Build from source
items.text:
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
python3 scripts/package_rustgis_plugin.py          # dist/topology-checker-<version>.rgplugin
node scripts/rustgis_plugin_smoke.mjs target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/rustgis-plugin/topology_checker_rustgis.wasm

crates/rustgis-plugin/plugin.json is generated from the rule registry, and a test fails when it is stale:

cargo run -p topology-checker-rustgis --example manifest > crates/rustgis-plugin/plugin.json

The plugin SDK needs Rust 1.90, newer than the workspace's 1.88, so the MSRV check skips this crate.

items.title: Web app
items.text:
topology-checker-web                 # http://127.0.0.1:8080
topology-checker-web --port 9000     # or TOPOLOGY_WEB_PORT=9000; 0 picks a free port

Install builds target/release/topology-checker-web. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only and rejects requests with another Host or Origin.

  1. Import a file of up to 512 MiB: GeoJSON, GeoPackage, FlatGeobuf, GeoParquet, KML, KMZ, GPX, or a zipped Shapefile. Or open one of the bundled examples.
  2. Choose layers, a working CRS, a tolerance and rules.
  3. Run the checks, then inspect violations in the table and on the map.
  4. Export violations as one violations layer with the CLI columns. GeoJSON, KML, KMZ and GPX use WGS84. GeoPackage, FlatGeobuf and GeoParquet use the working CRS. A JSON report is also available.
  5. Save a project zip to reopen the setup later.

Each browser tab has its own workspace. Workspaces idle for 4 hours are deleted.

Validation rows and their fixed-width row index are held in workspace-owned temporary files. Pagination and export use stable violation IDs without keeping the entire report in memory. Downloads stream directly through the browser's download manager. Invalid polygon input is reported with its feature and ring location, including invalid geometry retained in the original example datasets.

Polygon precision failures mark the validation job as failed and include its operation, rule and available source context in the job message. Temporary report rows are discarded; results and export endpoints remain unavailable for that job.
